current_activity: Market Garden: first flight lands six miles west of Arnhem, on the north bank of the Lower Rhine; about 5,700 men
notes: Event date: 17 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 35, 46). Event definition: On 17 September the first flight of the division lands outside Arnhem on the north bank of the Lower Rhine, its object being the road and rail bridges in the town, but the landing zones are six miles to the west in broken, wooded country; the troops landed include divisional headquarters, the 1st Parachute Brigade and most of the 1st Airlanding Brigade, some 5,700 men; the 2nd Parachute Battalion captures the north end of the road bridge at last light (pp. 35 and 38). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 35: "the first flight of the British 1st Airborne Division had been landed outside Arnhem, on the north bank of the Lower Rhine"; "the areas selected for landing (marked S, X and Z) were six miles away to the west"; p. 46: "The 1st Battalion crossed the railway at Wolfhezen station". Location: Wolfheze, Gelderland (new place), beside the landing zones with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Wolfheze, beside the landing zones S, X and Z; the page gives the distance and direction from Arnhem only. Location support: Ellis places the landing zones six miles west of Arnhem (p. 35) and the 1st Battalion crossing the railway at Wolfhezen station (p. 46).

current_activity: Withdraws across the Lower Rhine from the Oosterbeek perimeter during the night; about 2,000 of 7,500 come out
notes: Event date: the night of 25-26 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 39, 58, 97). Event definition: The division withdraws from Arnhem across the Lower Rhine during the night of 25-26 September, ending the Arnhem operation; General Eisenhower's message of thanks says it checked the German assault for nine days and came out some two thousand strong out of seven thousand five hundred; Ellis dates the withdrawal to the night of the 25th on p. 97 and gives the order as the 26th in Eisenhower's message on p. 58, so the later night is read as the one night 25-26 September (pp. 58 and 97; the perimeter at Hartenstein is named on p. 39). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 97: "withdrawal of the 1st Airborne Division from Arnhem during the night of September the 25th"; p. 58: "when, on 26th September, they were ordered to withdraw across the river"; p. 39: "Am forming perimeter defence at Hartenstein". Location: Oosterbeek, Gelderland (existing place PL0545), the perimeter with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Oosterbeek, the centre of the perimeter on the north bank of the Lower Rhine. Location support: Ellis names the perimeter at Hartenstein, in Oosterbeek (p. 39); the withdrawal is across the river there.
